MMGraphRAG is a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that constructs unified knowledge graphs spanning both textual and visual content, employing spectral clustering for multimodal entity analysis. It links scene graphs with textual representations, though this approach has been noted to suffer from structural blindness. As a baseline RAG framework, MMGraphRAG only adds basic image processing while treating tables and equations as plain text, thereby missing crucial structural information.

MMGraphRAG has been evaluated on several benchmarks. On the DocBench dataset, it achieved an overall accuracy of 61.0%, leading in the Academia, Government, and Unanswerable categories. On MMLongBench, it achieved an overall accuracy of 37.7%.

Beyond benchmark performance, MMGraphRAG has been examined in various failure and error cases. In a multi-panel figure interpretation case, it incorrectly identified VAE as having clearer separation. It incorrectly answered 11,503 million DKK for Novo Nordisk's wages and salaries in 2020. It provided a partially incorrect answer regarding the lowest accuracy GCAN configuration for Twitter15. It incorrectly identified the Bert-To-Bert model with an AUPRC of 0.708 as the highest performer for the Evidence Inference dataset. In a multimodal RAG failure case, it produced an incorrect answer about the NER label generation sequence. In a cross-modal noise case, it provided an incorrect answer regarding joint goal accuracy improvements in the Train domain.

LightRAG is a graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that integrates structured knowledge representation with dual-level retrieval mechanisms. It is an established text-centric extraction pipeline methodology referenced as a basis for constructing text-based knowledge graphs, and it employs a graph construction approach that uses sparsified indices to optimize structures for retrieval efficiency. As a baseline RAG framework, LightRAG is restricted to text-only content processing.

LightRAG has been evaluated on several benchmarks. On the DocBench dataset, it achieved an overall accuracy of 58.4% and led in the Law domain. On MMLongBench, it achieved an overall accuracy of 38.9%.

As a baseline model, LightRAG has also been assessed in various failure cases. It incorrectly identified VAE as having clearer separation in a multi-panel figure interpretation case, and it incorrectly answered DKK 11,503 million for Novo Nordisk's wages and salaries in 2020. It provided a partially incorrect answer regarding the lowest accuracy GCAN configuration for Twitter15, and it incorrectly identified the BERT + LSTM - Attention model with an AUPRC of 0.429 as the highest performer for the Evidence Inference dataset. In a multimodal RAG failure case, it produced an incorrect answer about the NER label generation sequence, and in a cross-modal noise case, it provided an incorrect answer regarding joint goal accuracy improvements in the Train domain.

GPT-4o-mini is a powerful multimodal language model with native text and image understanding capabilities and a 128K token context window. It serves as a backbone LLM and baseline in experimental frameworks, and is used to conduct all accuracy evaluations throughout these frameworks, ensuring consistent, reliable, and consistent assessment standards.

As a method, GPT-4o-mini was evaluated on the DocBench dataset, achieving an overall accuracy of 51.2%, and on MMLongBench, achieving an overall accuracy of 33.5%. As a baseline model, it demonstrated several incorrect responses across various tasks: it incorrectly identified VAE as having clearer separation in a multi-panel figure interpretation case; it incorrectly answered DKK 32,928 million for Novo Nordisk's wages and salaries in 2020; it provided an incorrect answer regarding the lowest accuracy GCAN configuration for Twitter15; and it incorrectly identified the BERT-to-BERT model with an AUPRC of 0.455 as the highest performer for the Evidence Inference dataset. Additionally, GPT-4o-mini was evaluated in a multimodal RAG failure case, producing an incorrect answer about the NER label generation sequence, and in a cross-modal noise case, providing an incorrect answer regarding joint goal accuracy improvements in the Train domain.

RAG-Anything is a unified, all-in-one retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework designed to reimagine multimodal knowledge representation and retrieval. It treats text, images, tables, and equations as first-class entities, reconceptualizing multimodal content as interconnected knowledge entities. The framework extends GraphRAG to all modalities and unifies heterogeneous multimodal knowledge by decomposing content into atomic content units.

At its core, RAG-Anything employs a dual-graph construction strategy, building both cross-modal and text-based knowledge graphs that are merged via entity alignment. This produces modality-aware graphs that preserve essential relationships within multimodal documents, enabling precise reasoning over complex layouts. Complementing this is a cross-modal hybrid retrieval mechanism, which together with the dual-graph approach forms the framework's central architecture for cross-modal retrieval and reasoning. The framework also includes a dense representation generation step in its indexing pipeline and constructs a cross-modal knowledge graph (as described by Equation 4). Additional features include context-aware multimodal prompting.

RAG-Anything demonstrates superior performance on long documents and complex multimodal layouts, particularly where relevant evidence is dispersed across multiple modalities and sections. It has been evaluated using the DocBench and MMLongBench benchmarks, including an ablation study on DocBench. On MMLongBench, it achieves the best results in information-dense domains such as Research Reports and Financial Reports, with consistent improvements across all document length categories: accuracy gains of 3.4 points for 11–50 pages, 9.3 points for 51–100 pages, and 7.9 points for 101–200 pages. It outperforms MM-GraphRAG on long-document reasoning tasks.

The framework excels at complex visual reasoning and tabular navigation by constructing structured graph representations of visual elements (such as bar plots) and tabular data, enabling precise alignment between visual and textual information. However, in documented failure cases, RAG-Anything produced an incorrect answer regarding the NER label generation sequence and failed to correctly interpret an irregular table in a cross-modal noise scenario. The framework's documentation also addresses challenges and future directions for multimodal RAG.

- Neighbor Text: 3.4 CASE STUDIES Multimodal documents contain rich structural information within each modality. Understanding these intra-modal structures is crucial for accurate reasoning. We analyze two representative cases from DocBench to demonstrate how RAG-Anything leverages these structures. These cases highlight a key limitation of existing methods. Baselines either rely on superficial textual cues or flatten complex visual elements into plain text. In contrast, RAG-Anything builds modality-aware graphs that preserve essential relationships (e.g., table header↔cell↔unit edges; panel↔caption↔axis edges). This enables precise reasoning over complex document layouts. • Case 1: Multi-panel Figure Interpretation. This case examines a common scenario in academic literature. Researchers often need to compare results across different experimental conditions. These results are typically presented in multi-panel visualizations. Figure 3 shows a challenging t-SNE visualization with multiple subpanels. The query requires distinguishing between two related but distinct panels. RAG-Anything constructs a visual-layout graph where panels, axis titles, legends, and captions become nodes. Key edges encode semantic relationships. Panels contain specific plots. Captions provide contextual information. Subfigures relate hierarchically. This structure guides the retriever to focus on the style-space panel for comparing cluster separation patterns. The system avoids confusion from the adjacent content space panel. This panel shows less clear distinctions. • Case 2: Financial Table Navigation. This case addresses a common challenge in financial document analysis. Analysts must extract specific metrics from tables with similar terminology and multiple time periods. Figure 4 shows this scenario. The query involves resolving ambiguous financial terms and selecting the correct column for a specified year. RAG-Anything transforms the financial report table into a structured graph. Each row header, column header (year), data cell, and unit becomes a node. The edges capture key relationships: row-of, column-of, header-applies-to, and unit-of. This structure enables precise navigation. The retriever focuses on the row “Wages and salaries” and the column for “2020”. It directs attention to the target cell (26,778 million). The system successfully disambiguates nearby entries like “Share-based payments.” Competing methods treat tables as linear text. They often confuse numerical spans and years. This leads to significantly inaccurate answers. RAG-Anything explicitly models relationships within the table. It achieves precise selection and numeric grounding. This ensures accurate responses.

Visual Analysis: The image is a horizontal composite figure illustrating a case study of multi-panel figure interpretation in multimodal document question answering. It is divided into three main sections: a left panel showing the source document and evidence, a middle panel showing baseline model responses, and a right panel showing additional baseline and the proposed model's response.

**Left Section: Multimodal Document and Evidence**
At the top left, a question is posed in a box: 'Question: Which model's style space shows a clearer separation between different styles according to Figure 2?' Below this, a small thumbnail of a multi-column academic paper is shown, labeled 'Multimodal Document'. A black arrow points from a highlighted region in the document to a larger inset labeled 'Evidence figure in the document'. This inset contains a two-panel t-SNE visualization. The left subpanel is labeled '(a) DAE' and shows two clusters (red and blue) that are somewhat overlapping. The right subpanel is labeled '(b) VAE' and shows two clusters (red and blue) that are more distinctly separated. Above the subpanels, text reads: '(DAE shows a clearer separation than VAE in Style Space)'. Below the subpanels, a caption reads: 'Figure 2: t-SNE plots of the disentangled style and content spaces on Yelp (with all auxiliary losses).' The left subpanel is annotated with 'Style Space' and the right with 'Content Space'.

**Middle Section: Baseline Model Responses**
The middle section contains two model responses, each with a model name and an emoji. The first is 'GPT-4o-mini 🤔:' followed by the text: 'According to Figure 2, the VAE model's style space shows a clearer separation between different styles.' The second is 'MMGraphRAG 🤔:' followed by: 'According to Figure 2, the model's style space shows a clearer separation between different styles in the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) compared to the Deterministic Autoencoder (DAE).' Both responses incorrectly identify VAE as having clearer separation.

**Right Section: Baseline and Proposed Model Responses**
The right section contains two more responses. The first is 'LightRAG 🤔:' followed by: 'According to Figure 2, the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) shows a clearer separation between different styles in its style space compared to the Deterministic Autoencoder (DAE).' This is also incorrect. The second is 'RAG-Anything(Correct ✅):' followed by: 'The DAE model's style space shows a clearer separation between different styles according to Figure 2.' This response is correct, as indicated by the green checkmark.

The figure demonstrates how RAG-Anything correctly interprets the multi-panel figure by focusing on the style-space panel (a) and avoiding confusion from the adjacent content-space panel (b), while baseline models fail. This aligns with the surrounding text describing Case 1: Multi-panel Figure Interpretation.
